hook_text: Two dams, 470 metres apart. At two in the morning the machines pump water up. At seven in the evening they let it fall. That is the grid's biggest battery, and here is how it and wind power work.
clip_script: Hydro: water falls through a pipe and spins a turbine; power is head times flow; ninety percent efficient, full power in a minute, but dams drown valleys and South Africa lacks big rivers, so we import from Cahora Bassa. Pumped storage: cheap night surplus pumps water up, the evening peak brings it down through the same machines; it loses a fifth but trades worthless power for precious power; three schemes, nearly 2700 megawatts. Wind: wing-shaped blades, power with the cube of speed, cheapest new power with solar, but a third of its rating on average. Pair wind and sun with pumped storage for the evening.
visual_style: Whiteboard dam cross-section with a penstock and runner; two reservoirs with arrows up at night and down at dusk; a wind turbine with a wing cross-section and a speed-cubed curve; a final mix diagram.
pacing: Hydro, our rivers, pumped storage, Ingula, wind, the mix.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and explain to someone why pumped storage pays despite losing energy.
